sourceName: Casino overnight parking, Reno/Sparks/Verdi and South Lake Tahoe/Stateline corridors -- second research pass. Mixed: operator-owned websites (primary) plus RV-community aggregators (casinocamper.com, Good Sam Camping blog) as clearly-labelled secondary sources; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim address geocoding.
method: Re-checked every casino named in the corridor brief plus the ones the first pass never looked at, and checked current operating status for each before checking any parking policy. Properties CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, with reasons: (1) Grand Sierra Resort, Reno -- resort is open but its own RV Park page reads 'Permanently Closed' as of 2026-08-12, and casinocamper.com reports overnight RV parking is no longer allowed in the free lot; excluded because the only sanctioned option there is gone. (2) Nugget Casino Resort, Sparks -- open, but casinocamper.com reports signage at the lot entrance stating overnight RV parking is not allowed. (3) Atlantis Casino Resort Spa, Reno -- open, but iOverlander lists it as 'Overnight Prohibited' and casinocamper.com reports overnight parking has not been allowed since 2017; reports conflict but all recent ones lean prohibited. (4) Peppermill, Reno -- open, but casinocamper.com says overnight is only 'maybe' allowed for registered hotel guests and Platinum-or-higher card holders, which is not a sleep spot for a passing driver. (5) Silver Legacy / Circus Circus / Eldorado (The Row) and other downtown Reno properties -- paid structured garages, no citable overnight-parking allowance found. (6) Harrah's and Harveys Lake Tahoe, Stateline -- both open, but the Harveys Outdoor Arena parking guide states RVs and semis may park at the back of the Harrah's garage and that 'Guests are not allowed to stay in the RV'; both went to year-round paid parking. (7) Bally's Lake Tahoe (formerly MontBleu, formerly Caesars Tahoe) and Golden Nugget Lake Tahoe (formerly Horizon, then Hard Rock Lake Tahoe) -- both OPEN and operating, correcting the first pass which recorded Horizon as permanently closed; it was rebranded, not closed. Neither publishes any overnight-parking or RV allowance, and both are inside the paid-parking regime imposed as a TRPA condition for the Tahoe South Events Center, so neither is included. (8) Lakeside Inn & Casino, Stateline -- permanently closed; the first pass was right to exclude it. (9) Bordertown Casino & RV Resort, US-395 north of Reno -- open with a real RV resort, but roughly 23 miles from the Reno endpoint, outside the ~15-mile corridor window. (10) Gold Dust West Casino & RV Park, Carson City -- open, paid RV park, but ~19 miles from South Lake Tahoe and ~25 from Reno, outside the window; a good candidate if a Carson City corridor pass is ever run. See policyNote -- the local-ordinance findings are the most important output of this pass, not the pin count.
policyNote: THREE JURISDICTIONS ON THESE CORRIDORS RESTRICT SLEEPING IN A PARKED VEHICLE, AND THE APP SHOULD NOT TREAT THEM AS NEUTRAL. (a) CITY OF SOUTH LAKE TAHOE, CA -- the city's camping ordinance (South Lake Tahoe City Code Chapter 4.70, Offenses Generally, effective 2019-06-06, now hosted at ecode360.com/SO4651) defines 'camp' to include sleeping, preparing to sleep, and laying down bedding, and expressly extends that definition to those activities conducted in a vehicle parked in a public space, public street, or private property, whether or not the engine is running. Retrieved 2026-08-12 via search-engine extracts of the code text plus a South Tahoe Now news report on adoption; the code host itself is behind a bot wall so the section-level text could not be fetched directly -- treat the exact section numbering as MEDIUM confidence, but the substance (vehicle sleeping is covered) is corroborated by two independent retrievals. NO SLEEP SPOTS SHOULD BE PLACED INSIDE THE CITY OF SOUTH LAKE TAHOE. (b) CITY OF RENO, NV -- Reno Municipal Code section 8.22.035 ('Nuisances per se defined') designates using any mobile home, recreational vehicle or vehicle for dwelling or sleeping purposes outside of a mobile home park, mobile home subdivision or recreational vehicle park as a nuisance per se. Reno has also had an overnight-parking restriction on the books since 1996, which it began actively enforcing against RVers in casino lots in September 2008 (Good Sam Camping blog, 'Casino Camping Update - Reno Nevada'). Retrieved 2026-08-12 from search-engine extracts of the Municode-hosted Reno Administrative Code; Municode is a JavaScript app and returned no fetchable text, so this is MEDIUM confidence on exact wording and HIGH confidence that a citywide restriction exists. Practical effect: casino lots inside Reno city limits are legally doubtful no matter what the casino's security desk tolerates. (c) DOUGLAS COUNTY, NV (which contains Stateline) -- Douglas County Code Title 9 contains Chapter 9.44, 'Illegal Camping', including section 9.44.030, 'Camping Outside Designated Area'. Confirmed 2026-08-12 that the chapter and section exist (Municode chapter listing and the Douglas County District Attorney's county-code index), but the operative text could NOT be retrieved -- Municode is bot-walled -- so it is unknown whether it reaches vehicles on private commercial property. UNRESOLVED, and it should be resolved before any Stateline pin is ever added. Two lower-risk jurisdictions for contrast: CITY OF SPARKS, NV limits its prohibition to public land -- Sparks Municipal Code Chapter 10.48 (section 10.48.250) makes it unlawful to dwell or sleep in a vehicle on a PUBLIC parking lot, which leaves private casino lots such as Baldini's outside the ban; and UNINCORPORATED WASHOE COUNTY, which covers Verdi, adopted a camping/vehicle-habitation ban on 2024-03-26 (Washoe County Code Chapters 50 and 70) that likewise applies to county-owned and public property, not to a private licensed RV resort. This is why the only new verified pin in this pass sits in Verdi and not in Reno, Sparks or Stateline.

records.name: Gold Ranch Casino & RV Resort -- Verdi
records.source: Gold Ranch Casino & RV Resort official site (RV Resort page)
records.notes: 350 Gold Ranch Rd, Verdi, NV 89439 -- I-80 exit 2, the first Nevada exit eastbound off Donner Pass and about 10 mi west of the Reno endpoint. This is a PAID, reservation-based RV resort attached to the casino, NOT free lot boondocking: 105 fully paved sites, 64 of them extra-wide pull-throughs, full hookups with 20/30/50 amp, wi-fi at every site. Rates posted on the operator's own site on 2026-08-12 for the summer season (May 1 - Sept 30, 2026): $60 back-in / $65 pull-through Mon-Thu, $65 / $70 Fri-Sun, premium sites $70-75, and $85-100 during Hot August Nights (Jul 30 - Aug 9). Valid credit card required, 48-hour cancellation notice or you are charged one night. Reservations (775) 345-8880. Amenities: remodeled restrooms, laundry, clubhouse with fireplace, seasonal heated pool, year-round jacuzzi, pet-friendly (up to two dogs), 24-hour convenience store, Sinclair gas station, three food options on site. RELEVANT TO AN EV: there is a 16-stall Tesla V3 Supercharger (up to 250 kW, open to non-Tesla EVs via NACS/CCS adapter, 24 hours) at this same 350 Gold Ranch Rd address, confirmed 2026-08-12 via OpenStreetMap POI plus PlugShare and DCFC Tracker listings -- so this is one of the few spots on the corridor where you can charge and legally sleep on the same lot. JURISDICTION: unincorporated Washoe County, not Reno city, so the Reno vehicle-dwelling nuisance ordinance does not apply, and Washoe County's 2024 camping ban covers public/county property rather than a licensed private RV park. CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the resort operating, its rates and its legality -- all from the operator's own current site. Lot lighting and overnight noise are not stated by the operator; it sits immediately alongside I-80, so expect freeway noise. Not an anonymous pull-in-and-sleep spot: you check in like a campground.

records.name: Bonanza Casino -- Reno
records.source: casinocamper.com RV-community listing and user report (secondary, undated listing)
records.notes: 4720 N Virginia St, Reno, NV 89506 -- north Reno on US-395, about 3 mi from the Reno endpoint. Property status confirmed CURRENTLY OPERATING and open 24 hours on 2026-08-12 (Yelp and the casino's own site; 24-hour Branding Iron Cafe on site, so there is somewhere to sit at 3am). Overnight parking: casinocamper.com lists overnight RV parking as allowed, with a user report saying to park by the back wall up a slight hill behind employee parking, to let security know you are staying, and that one night is OK. The same report says the lot is NOT level and the usable area is small -- bad for a big rig, fine for a car. LEGAL WARNING, READ BEFORE USING THIS PIN: this lot is inside CITY OF RENO limits, and Reno Municipal Code section 8.22.035 declares using any vehicle for dwelling or sleeping purposes outside a licensed RV park to be a nuisance per se; Reno has also enforced a 1996 overnight-parking restriction against RVers in casino lots since 2008. Casino security tolerating you does not make the city ordinance go away. CONFIDENCE: LOW. The permission side rests on a single undated community listing with one user report; the ordinance side rests on search-engine extracts of the Municode-hosted code that could not be fetched directly. Deliberately left verified:false. Phone the casino at (775) 323-2724 and ask security before committing, and prefer casino-gold-ranch-verdi-nv (paid, legal, 10 mi west on I-80) if you have the option.
